name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "The charge reversal E1021K sits on a membrane-facing surface of the catalytic-domain helix and adds a positive charge that strengthens electrostatic contact with the anionic PIP2-containing membrane, increasing membrane association and lipid kinase output.", "mechanism_class": "ligand_binding", "supports": ["E2", "E3", "E5", "E9"], "would_refute": "Residue 1021 is buried or faces away from the membrane-binding surface in the AlphaFold model and in all 20 experimental structures, with no lipid head group or ligand within contact distance; or electrostatic surface calculations show no change in the membrane-facing potential after E\u2192K.", "starting_rank": 1, "rank_rationale": "E2 is the only record item that names a mechanism for this exact residue, describing enhanced membrane association and kinase activity, which fits a lipid-contact change. E5 and E9 tie APDS1 p110delta mutations to oncogenic p110alpha activation, which works through membrane binding. Weaknesses: E2 describes a gain of function, not the loss of function in the task premise (E13 also says gain). G1 leaves residue position unconfirmed and G5 means no mutant structure exists, so this is untested. Missing: a residue-level structural placement of E1021 and a membrane-binding assay for E1021K."}

name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "E1021 forms part of the interface with the p85 regulatory subunit; the charge reversal weakens the p85 (iSH2) restraint on p110delta, so the catalytic subunit is released from inhibition and becomes constitutively active.", "mechanism_class": "protein_interaction", "supports": ["E19", "E9", "E5", "E13"], "would_refute": "In p110delta\u2013p85 complex structures or docking models, residue 1021 has no atom within contact distance of the p85 regulatory subunit, and E\u2192K leaves the predicted p85 binding energy unchanged or stronger.", "starting_rank": 2, "rank_rationale": "E19 confirms that PIK3CD is a heterodimer with p85, and E9 shows that p85 mutations activate p110delta strongly. That makes disrupted p85 restraint a plausible route to gain of function. It ranks below ligand_binding because no record item places E1021 at the p85 interface, and E5 concerns oncogenic activation in general rather than this residue. The p85 complex is absent from the 20 structures in E15, so this is untested. Missing: a p110delta\u2013p85 complex model and the residue's contacts in it."}

arguments: {"statement": "The charge reversal breaks an intramolecular salt bridge or contact between the 1008\u20131031 helix and the adjacent domain of the same p110delta chain, destabilising the autoinhibited conformation and shifting the catalytic domain toward the active state.", "mechanism_class": "domain_interface", "supports": ["E3", "E4", "E17", "E8", "E14"], "would_refute": "In the AlphaFold model and the 20 experimental structures, residue 1021 makes no side-chain contact with another domain of the same chain (no partner atom within about 4 \u00c5), and molecular dynamics of wild type versus E1021K shows no change in the interdomain distance or helix position.", "starting_rank": 3, "rank_rationale": "The helix at 1008\u20131031 (E3) sits in a well-predicted region (E17, mean pLDDT 87.94). Pathogenicity scores (E8 0.975, E14 0.681) and conservation (E10 0.918) show the residue matters, but none of them says where it contacts the chain. An interdomain contact is possible and consistent with the p110alpha analogy in E5, but it is the least supported of the three because the record contains no contact data. It also conflicts with the loss-of-function premise, since this mechanism would more naturally produce gain of function. Missing: the contact map for residue 1021 (G1, G5), and a stability calculation for E1021K."}
